doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing on Alice Coltrane's Universal Consciousness
summary: He recalls recording at the Coltranes' Queens house studio.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: And before we return to following your ensemble, Directions, I wanted to also just comment on a couple recordings that weren’t under your name but again were very influential. The date with Alice Coltrane, Universal Consciousness. How did that come about?
Well, I think she called me to come out to the house in Queens.
Is that the same house that…
Yeah. They tried to get the historical landmark.
Yeah, they had a studio in the house so I came out and played on a few tracks. I think Cecil McBee was on it.
And a string quartet, violins, strings. Leroy Jenkins.
Which was… Did Ornette do the strings or did she write the strings?
It’s not crediting any of the arrangement, I just noticed that Leroy Jenkins is in the string section.
